defect.problem: The good-law status can survive as the lake's ultimate judgment, but the content page's blanket 'No negative treatment' statement is too strong. The disclosed treatment edges include proposed negative-treatment signals, including questioned labels and one superseded_by_statute label, even though those edges are classified as mentioned/proposed.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep the status as good only with qualification, and replace 'No negative treatment' with language such as: 'No controlling negative treatment identified in the disclosed record; disclosed progeny includes proposed questioned/superseded signals classified as mentioned, so verify citing cases before relying on an unqualified current-treatment statement.'

reasons: The lake's ultimate field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30, so the status is not refuted outright from the disclosed record.

The same lake record discloses proposed treatment edges: Chavez, Braxton, O'Neil, and Elmore are labeled questioned; Tolbert is labeled superseded_by_statute; all are field_iii=mentioned and proposed=true.
Provenance also warns that treatment.field_i_validity came from migration/page frontmatter, so an unqualified 'No negative treatment' statement overstates the disclosed treatment record.
residual_risks: Underlying citing-case texts are not present, so the disclosed record supports softening the page but not a definitive downgrade beyond the lake's good_law judgment.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Change the subsequent-history bullet from 'No negative treatment' to 'No controlling negative treatment identified in the disclosed record; proposed citing-case signals require verification.'
